Prepare a count history as input for abundance and occupancy models

Source: R/07_model_input.R
pam_model_input.Rd

Turns a count history into the pieces that site-occupancy and abundance models use: the response y (sites by occasions), the site covariates siteCovs and the observation covariates obsCovs. It handles one species or several, and one season or several. pamflow does not fit these models; use the prepared input with the package you prefer, such as unmarked, ubms or spOccupancy.

Usage

pam_model_input(
  history,
  binary = FALSE,
  standardize = FALSE,
  drop_unsurveyed = TRUE,
  seasons = NULL,
  season_covariates = NULL,
  dir = NULL
)

Arguments

history

A pam_count_history from pam_count_history() or pam_as_count_history(), or a pam_count_histories from pam_count_histories().

binary

If FALSE (the default), y holds the counts, as used by N-mixture (abundance) models. If TRUE, y is detection (1) or non-detection (0), as used by occupancy and Royle-Nichols models.

standardize

If TRUE, numeric covariates are centered and scaled (mean 0, standard deviation 1), which helps models converge. The center and scale are returned in scaling so that new data can be treated the same way. Default FALSE: covariates are returned as they are.

drop_unsurveyed

If TRUE (the default), sites with no surveyed occasion are left out of every piece, because model functions cannot use them.

seasons

Optional data frame with the columns season (a name), start and end (Dates) that groups the occasions into seasons (primary periods) for multi-season models; see pam_define_seasons(). An occasion belongs to the season that contains its first day. Occasions outside every season are left out; seasons with fewer occasions than the longest are padded with NA.

season_covariates

Optional data frame with a season column and one column per covariate that changes between seasons but not between sites (for example rainfall or year); needs seasons.

dir

Optional folder. If given, the pieces are also written there as CSV files, for use outside R. Nothing is written by default.

Value

An object of class pam_model_input. For one species and no seasons it is a list with

  • y: integer matrix, sites in rows and occasions in columns, NA where a site was not surveyed;

  • siteCovs: data frame of site covariates, one row per site (row names are the site identifiers); NULL if there are none;

  • obsCovs: named list of matrices shaped like y: effort (recorded hours, when the history has it) and day (days since the first occasion);

  • site_ids, species, count, binary;

  • scaling: center and scale of every standardized covariate.

With several species, y is an array (species, sites, occasions) and species lists the species. With seasons, the list also has

  • y_array: sites x seasons x occasions within season (with a leading species dimension for several species); y is then the wide matrix sites x (seasons * occasions) for one species, and NULL for several;

  • obsCovs (wide matrices) and obsCovs_array (arrays), shaped like y and y_array;

  • num_primary (number of seasons), n_secondary (occasions per season, including padding), seasons (with the number of occasions found) and occasion_map (which original occasion went where);

  • with season_covariates: yearlySiteCovs (data frame, one row per site and season, sites first) and yearlySiteCovs_matrices (sites x seasons).

The layout of y is stored in attr(x, "layout"); pam_check_model_input() uses it.

Details

Using the result with unmarked or ubms

Both build their data frames from these pieces:

x <- pam_model_input(history)
umf <- unmarked::unmarkedFramePCount(y = x$y, siteCovs = x$siteCovs, obsCovs = x$obsCovs)
fit <- unmarked::pcount(~ effort ~ canopy, data = umf, K = 100)

x <- pam_model_input(history, binary = TRUE)
umf <- unmarked::unmarkedFrameOccu(y = x$y, siteCovs = x$siteCovs, obsCovs = x$obsCovs)
fit <- unmarked::occu(~ effort ~ canopy, data = umf)

# several seasons
x <- pam_model_input(history, binary = TRUE, seasons = pam_define_seasons(history))
umf <- unmarked::unmarkedMultFrame(y = x$y, siteCovs = x$siteCovs, obsCovs = x$obsCovs,
                                   numPrimary = x$num_primary)

The detection formula (before the second ~) may use the observation covariates effort and day and any site covariate; the other formula uses site covariates. ubms takes the same unmarkedFrame* objects.

Using the result with spOccupancy

spOccupancy expects a list with the response, the occupancy covariates and the detection covariates, which are the same pieces under other names (check the argument names against its documentation):

x <- pam_model_input(history, binary = TRUE)          # one species
data <- list(y = x$y, occ.covs = x$siteCovs, det.covs = x$obsCovs,
             coords = coords)   # coords: your site coordinates, same row order

x <- pam_model_input(histories, binary = TRUE)        # several species
data <- list(y = x$y, occ.covs = x$siteCovs, det.covs = x$obsCovs, coords = coords)

For several species y has the species first (species x sites x occasions). With seasons use y_array and obsCovs_array. x$site_ids gives the site order.

About counts

Counts are numbers of detections, not numbers of animals. A model fitted to them gives a relative abundance index, not a population size. N-mixture models also slow down when counts are large (the upper bound K must exceed the highest count), so count = "files" in pam_count_history() or shorter occasions are often better than raw event counts.

Site covariates with missing values cannot be used by model functions; a warning names them.

See also

pam_count_history(), pam_count_histories(), pam_define_seasons(), pam_check_model_input()

Examples

counts <- matrix(c(0, 2, 5, 1, 0, 3, 4, 0, 2, 1, 1, 0), nrow = 3,
                 dimnames = list(c("site_a", "site_b", "site_c"), NULL))
hist <- pam_as_count_history(counts, site_covariates = data.frame(canopy = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.9)),
                             effort = matrix(24, 3, 4), species = "Example species")
#> Error in pam_as_count_history(counts, site_covariates = data.frame(canopy = c(0.2,     0.5, 0.9)), effort = matrix(24, 3, 4), species = "Example species"): could not find function "pam_as_count_history"
x <- pam_model_input(hist)
#> Error in pam_model_input(hist): could not find function "pam_model_input"
x$y
#> Error: object 'x' not found
x$siteCovs
#> Error: object 'x' not found
names(x$obsCovs)
#> Error: object 'x' not found
# detection / non-detection instead of counts, covariates standardized
pam_model_input(hist, binary = TRUE, standardize = TRUE)$y
#> Error in pam_model_input(hist, binary = TRUE, standardize = TRUE): could not find function "pam_model_input"
